groups.title: checker.py: checks a text submission against a quest's acceptance criteria and sets the exit code

checks.why: the checker against the summary quest, pass and fail

risks.text: An unknown criterion type silently counts as failed (ok = False), so a new type in a quest fails every submission until checker.py handles it.
check() reads quest["acceptance_criteria"], c["type"] and c["description"] directly; a quest missing any of these raises KeyError instead of reporting a failure.
Callers script against the exit code (0 only if every criterion passes) and the PASS/FAIL lines; changing either breaks anything that wraps checker.py.

groups.title: Quest definitions in JSON: a title plus acceptance_criteria that checker.py evaluates

checks.why: summary.json is loaded and checked by the tests

risks.text: Criterion "type" must be one of contains, max_chars, min_chars as handled in checker.py; any other value always fails.
tests/test_checker.py reads quests/summary.json and expects a 280-char limit and a "Source:" line; editing it breaks those tests. tagline.json has no test.

groups.title: License and README describing the demo and how to run it
pytest tests for checker.py using the real quest files

risks.text: A green pytest run says little about the tagline quest, min_chars or an unknown criterion type: only summary.json is exercised, so a broken tagline.json or new criterion type still passes.

rules.rule: Every quest must have at least one checkable acceptance criterion.
rules.why: A quest with none would pass every submission vacuously (all([]) is True), so nothing is actually checked. Nothing enforces this automatically: pytest only loads summary.json, so check any new or edited quest by hand.

checks.why: runs checker.py against summary.json; does not cover tagline.json, so review new quests by hand

rules.rule: Every criterion type used in quests/ must be implemented in checker.py.
rules.why: Unhandled types always fail, so the quest becomes impossible to pass.
